headline: Transfer of $750,000 from the Cannabis Stabilization account to Ezekiel's Plan 2.0.
summary: The committee will consider the $750,000 transfer, along with noise at Wyckoff Country Club and possible changes to the city's noise rules in Chapter 83. Other items cover sidewalk and drainage problems, traffic on Old Jarvis Ave, and a proposed Lived Experience Committee.

plain_text:
Published October 15, 2026, 1:42 p.m.
City Council
Holyoke Massachusetts
Pursuant to the Massachusetts Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25,
and Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025,
notice is hereby given of a meeting of the committee on
Public Safety
Monday, October 19, 2026
6:30 PM
Meeting to take place at
Holyoke City Hall, 536 Dwight Street
and can be accessed remotely on Zoom Meetings
Per order of the Chair: Anne Thalheimer
Remote access via zoom.us
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81144139549?pwd=CMyBWUHb2hNgSHb961r0yORoYFVzbK.1
Meeting ID: 811 4413 9549 Meeting Passcode: 565897 or by call in at 1 (646) 558-8656 with
the same Meeting ID and Passcode.
Live Spanish interpretation will be available on local access channel 15 using the television's
SAP option, through the live stream on the city website, as well as on the Zoom feed by clicking
the interpretation option and choosing Spanish.
Agenda
Item 1: 11-6-25 From Holyoke Residents-letter to Mayor Garcia regarding noise at Wyckoff
Country Club
*Tabled 4-13-26
Item 2: 11-18-25 From Residents in Ward 7-Neighborhood Petition to Address Noise
Complaints
*Tabled 4-13-26
Item 3: 4-21-26 Thalheimer, Panitch, Devine - Request HPD to provide the Public Safety
committee with a copy of any and all current/active loudspeaker permit applications for Wyckoff
Country Club (with any personally identifying information such as DOB and SSN etc. redacted).
*Tabled 6-8-26
Item 4: 4-21-26 Thalheimer, Panitch, Devine - Request License Board to provide the Public
Safety committee with a copy of any and all current/active Entertainment permit applications for
Wyckoff Country Club (with any personally identifying information such as DOB and SSN etc.
redacted), including a list of any conditions attached to said permit(s), if any.
*Tabled 6-8-26
Item 5: 9-15-26 DEVINE - Ordered, that there be and is hereby appropriated by transfer in the
fiscal year 2027, SEVEN HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND 00/100 Dollars ($750,000.00) as
follows:
FROM
8815-10400 CANNABIS STABILIZATION $750,000.00
TOTAL $750,000.00
TO:
19442-57087 EZEKIEL'S PLAN 2.0 $750,000.00
TOTAL $750,000.00
*Referred from Finance Committee 10-6-26
LAID ON THE TABLE
(Items taken up at previous meeting(s) and laid on the table.
Item 6: 8-1-23 BARTLEY, DEVINE, J. RIVERA - Ordered, The City Engineer and/or VEOLIA
suggest improvements to the sidewalk and catch basin near 5 Martin St. (at the corner of
Westfield Rd and Martin). Owner's contractor noted the sidewalk is too high and the design
causes water to pool on parking lot; the catch basin is above-grade is not catching storm water.
Owner very willing to confer with City Engineer on this matter. Refer to Public Safety
Committee for a review hearing.
*Tabled 12-30-24, 3-31-25, 12-15-25, 3-9-26, 8-10-26
Item 7: 9-4-24 BARTLEY, J. RIVERA - (copy) The DPW install a protective wraparound barrier
(lattice, wire) the Holyoke Railroad platform. Unfortunately people are using this for protection
from the elements but it is a very dangerous location and I don't want anyone to stumble onto
the rail tracks as recently happened in Northampton.
*Tabled 12-30-24, 3-13-25, 12-15-25, 3-9-26, 8-10-26
Item 8: 1-6-26 Thalheimer- The condition of the sidewalk on Northampton St between West
Glen and Clark Streets is virtually impassable especially for persons with disabilities.
*Tabled 3-9-26
Item 9: 1-6-26 Anderson-Burgos - Ordered that the City Engineer review Old Jarvis Ave to
address traffic safety concerns of several residents, including vehicles traveling at high speeds
and large trucks traveling on the street on a regular basis. Residents are asking for
consideration of a truck exclusion, making it a one way, and/or barriers at one end making it a
dead end. Residents have expressed that speed humps were installed 15 years ago, but they
did not prevent speeding.
*Tabled 3-9-26, 8-10-26
Item 10: 3-3-26 I. Rivera - Order that the honorable city council in collaboration with the Mayor
create a Lived Experience Committee (LEC) that would assist in advising the city regarding
community efforts around topics of Homelessness, Substance Use Disorder, Education and
Quality of Life issues.
This committee is to be comprised of Holyoke residents hailing from all 7 wards capturing
representation from all over the city.
*Tabled 6-8-26, 8-10-26
Item 11: 4-21-26 Panitch, Thalheimer: Ordered, That the Council revisit and comprehensively
revise the noise provisions of Chapter 83 of the Holyoke Code of Ordinances to reflect
contemporary circumstances and address noise issues in the City of Holyoke.
*Tabled 8-10-26
ADMINISTRATIVELY LAID ON THE TABLE
(Per City Council Rule 9P, "Any order not acted on within 45 business days shall be deemed
tabled." Items within this section are laid on the table by virtue of being in the committee more
than 45 days.)
Item 12: 12-16-25 Magrath-Smith - Ordered, that a monthly standing order be added to Public
Safety meetings where the committee reviews the See-Click-Fix Report and the status of
logged issues.
Item 13: 12-16-25 Magrath-Smith - Ordered, that a plan be presented to Public Safety
concerning how See-Click-Fix can be effectively implemented through DPW, Engineering, and
Council, including how it can be made prominent on the city website, how councilors can log
issues from constituents, what communication structure can be used to respond to people who
log issues, and how a public-facing report can be shared online showing the status of issues
that were logged. Consider also if a "Driving Speed/Traffic Complaint" category can be added.
Item 14: 2-3-26 Vacon- ORDER: that the HPD, HFD & DPW provide a quarterly summary (no
individual information) report to the city council on employee injuries including; number of
employees out injured, length of time out, & nature of injuries & any actions taken to reduce
injuries, along with any other information the department wishes to include. Refer to Public
Safety & copy to each department.
Item 15: 6-16-26 Thalheimer, Purcell - Invite Roca Holyoke to an upcoming Public Safety
meeting for a conversation highlighting the work that they are doing in Holyoke to disrupt
violence by engaging young people, police, and systems to heal trauma, find hope, and drive
change.
Administrative Assistant: Jeffery Anderson-Burgos
The listing of matters are those reasonably anticipated by the chair which may be discussed at
the meeting. Not all items listed may in fact be discussed and other items may also be brought
up for discussion to the extent permitted by law. Agenda subject to change up to two business
days (48 hours) prior to posted meeting time.
